name: nml-lang
description: Schema-aware editing for the NML configuration language: diagnostics, quick fixes, completions, hovers and formatting from a bundled language server

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In an untrusted workspace the neutral nml-lsp still validates committed and cached schema (NML is data, not code). A project's own tool language server (`<tool> lsp`) is only launched once you trust the workspace.

walkthroughs.title: Get schema-aware NML editing
walkthroughs.description: Validate NML config against its schema, with completions and hovers.

steps.title: Open an NML file
steps.description:
Open any `.nml` file — the bundled language server starts by itself; there is nothing to install. The status bar (bottom-right) names the schema package governing the file, or says `nml: no schema`; hover it for the content hash (`blake3:{hash8}`), the schema's source, binding and server. Errors, quick fixes, completions and hovers come from that schema.
[Open a folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)

steps.title: Use your tool's schema (optional)
steps.description:
If your project is built with a schema-provider tool (e.g. nudge), declare it in `nml-project.nml`:

```
project MyApp:
    provider:
        tool = "nudge"
```

In a trusted workspace the editor then validates against the exact tool binary — zero sync. Otherwise the neutral server serves the tool's published package.

steps.title: Use a native server (optional)
steps.description:
The extension ships the neutral `nml-lsp` server as WebAssembly, so nothing needs installing. To run a native build instead — a very large tree, or a machine where the WASI host extension cannot run — point `nml.server.path` at an `nml-lsp` binary outside your workspace (until the crates.io release, `cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/nudge-io/nml nml-lsp` puts one at `~/.cargo/bin/nml-lsp`).
[Open NML settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22nml.server%22)

semanticTokenTypes.description: Unit suffix of a duration literal (RFC 0017). Falls back to number coloring in themes without a specific rule.

nml.server.path.description: Absolute path to a native nml-lsp binary to run instead of the bundled WebAssembly server (a leading ~/ expands to your home directory; other relative paths are refused). Leave it empty — the default — to use the bundled server. Machine-scoped on purpose: a workspace cannot set it, and a path inside an open workspace folder is refused, so a repository can never point the editor at a binary it ships.

nml.trace.server.description: Log LSP protocol messages to the NML Language Server Trace output channel. Off by default.
